messages:
From: Jared Wilson <jared.wilson@finworks.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up (FinWorks)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — good conversation. A couple quick clarifying points from our side as we scope the Private deployment: 

- Primary goal: host inference inside our AWS account so customer data never traverses public Redwood endpoints.
- Network options we discussed: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering. Our infra team prefers PrivateLink for tighter control, but they're open to Peering if there are perf tradeoffs.
- We will need an IP allowlist on Redwood side for any management/control plane IPs and the ability to pin model versioning for auditability.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports PrivateLink for Private deployments (cross-account NLB + endpoints) and what CIDR/IP ranges you'd need from us? Also curious about whether you require any inbound rules or just expect us to initiate connections to your endpoints.

I'll loop in our IT alias for network details once we have the ask.

Thanks,
Jared
Director of Product
FinWorks

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Wilson <jared.wilson@finworks.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up (FinWorks)

Hi Jared — great talking earlier, appreciate the clarity. Short answers up front:

- Yes, Redwood Private supports both AWS PrivateLink (customer VPC endpoints to our NLB) and VPC Peering. PrivateLink is our recommended pattern when customers want strict control and a one-way, managed connectivity model.
- For PrivateLink we provide a stable NLB hostname and our recommended outbound IP ranges for management/control plane interactions. For peering we ask for your VPC CIDR and we’ll coordinate route table updates.
- We can support IP allowlists for the control plane and the management endpoints; you can also pin model versions and turn on audit logging for inference requests.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Quick 30-min network alignment call with your infra (Jared + FinWorks IT) + our infra engineer (Sean) tomorrow to walk diagrams and confirm whether PrivateLink or Peering is better given your constraints.
2) I'll attach a high-level network diagram and our Private VPC setup guide so your team can review before the call.
3) If Procurement needs an initial SOW/quote, Stephanie will follow up after we confirm the topology.

Proposed times: Tue 2026-07-21 10:00am PT or Tue 2026-07-21 2:00pm PT — which works for you?

Attachments: finworks_vpc_network_diagram.pdf (stub), redwood_private_vpc_setup_guide.pdf (stub)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up (FinWorks)

Marissa / Sean,

Thanks for the materials — quick technical notes from our networking team before the call: 

- We prefer AWS PrivateLink to avoid broad route propagation, but we have two constraints: 1) our EKS cluster requires 10.0.0.0/16 and our security team is strict on allowed endpoints; 2) any management/control plane IPs must be documented and static if possible.
- Can Redwood provide a minimal set of CIDR/IPs per region for the control plane and NLB? We need that for our security review.
- Regarding inbound vs outbound: we prefer initiating outbound connections to Redwood-managed endpoints (PrivateLink supports that), but we need to confirm TLS mutual auth options and whether Redwood requires any inbound ports opened on our side.

We'll join the 10:00am PT slot tomorrow — Jared, please send the calendar invite to the infra alias and include the network diagram.

— Priya (on behalf of FinWorks IT)
Network Operations Lead
FinWorks

Thanks everyone for jumping on the call this morning — great alignment. Recap and agreed next steps: 

- Topology: Customer prefers AWS PrivateLink (confirmed) for control plane isolation. Redwood will provision an NLB per-region and provide a stable hostname.
- IPs/CIDR: Sean to provide the list of outbound IPs we use for control plane and NLB health checks by EOD tomorrow. These will be CIDR blocks where possible; we’ll flag any single-IP requirements.
- Auth & Ports: Redwood supports TLS mutual auth for management operations; no inbound ports required on FinWorks side beyond the endpoint creation for PrivateLink.
- Model pinning & audit: Redwood will enable model version pinning and audit logging for the initial rollout.
- Procurement: Stephanie will send a preliminary SOW and quote based on the PrivateLink topology and expected rps. Procurement (procurement@finworks.com) to confirm budget window.

Action owners and timeline: 
- Sean Gallagher (Redwood infra): outbound IP list + NLB hostname by 2026-07-23 EOD.
- Marissa Cole (Redwood): coordinate SOW handoff to Stephanie.
- Stephanie Nguyen (Redwood): SOW & quote to FinWorks Procurement by 2026-07-24.
- FinWorks IT: validate IP/CIDR against security policy by 2026-07-27.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FW-2026-07) | SOW draft (DocuSign link will be shared by Stephanie)
